observations: The installed worker received an authenticated subscription search. Douban signed search, Bangumi subject search and AniList GraphQL each contributed a same-title card item in source priority order, despite reversed source settings.
The third item triggered exactly one AniList detail request for 777 before any TMDB identity lookup. No Douban or Bangumi detail request was made.

The actual host saved season one against TMDB 123, delivered the subscription notice and committed SubscribeAdded. The sealed creation origin retained the pair anilist:777 and TMDB 123, plus anilist_id=777 in the source MediaInfo.
The isolated App stopped. Prior movie, TV, transfer and slash cases were not run again.

prior_fixture_failures.observation: All three results and the selected callback reached the host. The restrictive TMDB fixture blocked season-one detail during actual subscription creation. The final fixture supplied that response on the same loopback service.

adaptations_and_open_in_scope: A non-TMDB card keeps an opaque provider ID, then uses an exact same-provider detail response and the existing unique TMDB identity bridge. Native library, download and subscription IDs remain TMDB-scoped; source-attribution records preserve the independent provider ID. The ordinary subscription runtime DTO still projects native media_source as TMDB. An absent or ambiguous link prevents mutation.

Named provider genre IDs remain unchanged in the original JSON model; the native display uses their names. The native provider request/caching layer retains its bounded transport and safe media image handling. No live provider traffic or production message was sent.

This run verifies search across all three alternate providers and actual AniList subscription. Direct Douban/Bangumi subscription, non-TMDB download, a provider failure continuing to the next provider, cold recovery and other source-specific edge cases were not exercised. Multi-season packages and the remaining /subscribes and Lark worker gaps remain open.
